why: Each position is used at most once and you need an exact total: that is 0/1 knapsack with feasibility only, reach[s] = can some subset of the items seen so far sum to s. The 2-D table (items x sum) collapses to one row iterated from high sums to low.
hints: You only need to know which sums are reachable, not which items made them (until the follow-up).
reach[s] after item v = reach[s] or reach[s - v]; iterate s downward so v is used at most once. A Python big-integer bitset does the same with reach |= reach << v.
O(n * target) = 4*10^6 booleans. For the follow-up, keep the 2-D table (or record for each sum which item first reached it) and walk back from target.
pitfalls: Iterating sums upward turns this into unbounded knapsack (an item reused).
Values larger than target can be skipped; equal values at different positions are separate items.
Mask the bitset to target + 1 bits or it grows needlessly.
